newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Franc under pressure, Euro shares quiet.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Franc under pressure, Euro shares quiet.

text.p: The French franc drifted perilously close to its old European Exchange Rate Mechanism floor against the mark on Thursday, prompting the Bank of France to try to prop it up.
Early trade in the dollar and European shares was thin, traders said.
The mark spiked up to 3.4315 francs overnight, its strongest level since March 22, and dealers said the French central bank intervened to buy francs at 3.4300 in early European business.

A larger-than-expected increase in German second-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) dealt an extra blow to the franc after Wednesday's data showing the French economy shrank more than had been expected in the second quarter.

"This has been triggered by the GDP report from Germany which has been a lot stronger than forecast and contrasts quite sharply with what's going on in France," said Michael Lewis, senior international economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
The franc was at 3.4287 per mark in mid-morning trade, compared with Wednesday's late European level of 3.4280. Its old Exchange Rate Mechanism floor was 3.4305 per mark.
"The BoF is doing a smoothing operation rather than trying to reverse the trend. It's all being done through French banks and volume doesn't appear to be large," said one trader.
Analysts said the market would keep hammering at the franc at least until the 1997 budget was officially presented on September 18. Key details of the budget plans are already known.
German second-quarter GDP rose 1.5 percent on the quarter, compared to consensus forecasts of 1.1 percent and a first-quarter fall of 0.5 percent.
That compares with France's 0.4 percent quarter-on-quarter GDP drop, down from a 1.1 percent rise in the first quarter.

The Bank of France monetary policy council meets during the morning with the results, due at 1115 GMT, not forecast to reveal any change in policy. Germany's Bundesbank council is also in session and markets expect no interest rate change there.
Meanwhile, the dollar was quoted at 1.4820 marks and 108.90 yen, little changed from its late European levels on Wednesday.
European share prices were were mostly firmer in early trade on the back of Wall Street's 8.51 point gain on Wednesday.
But fears over Friday's U.S. jobs report -- seen as a significant indicator of the trend in the Federal Reserve's interest rate policy -- were seen keeping a cap on prices.
"It's hard to see anyone doing much in front of the non-farm payrolls," said one trader in London.
Yet he said British fund managers were flush with cash and could be tempted to increase their equity holdings at the end of a strong period for British shares.
French stocks opened higher as investors were encouraged by a rash of good corporate results -- notably from Danone and Carrefour.
Traders said the market was waiting for Prime Minister Alain Juppe's tax reform address this evening. They said the market did not expect French or German interest rate cuts.
German shares opened steady, shrugging off a small rise in German jobless data for August but with buying limited before the Bundesbank meeting and Friday's U.S. jobs figures.
CURRENCIES AT 0930 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4820 marks and 108.90 yen after 1.4815 marks and 108.08 yen late on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0930 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 3.9 points at 3,876.6.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX index was down 2.56 at 2,529.83.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 8.28 at 1,993.05.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $386 an ounce, compared with $385.65 late on Wednesday.
